title: Training Note: Returned-Payment Concession in the Payoff of a Past-Due Invoice (Contingency Placement Agreements)
content:
**What is the returned-payment concession?**
In the payoff of a past-due fee invoice of an agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements, a returned-payment concession applies by the collections reversed as returned payments on the agreement in the 3 months before the payoff, because those reversals delay the client's reconciliation of its fee invoices: 10 percent for 2 or more, 5 percent for exactly one, and nothing for none.

**Which reversals count?**
Reversal entries in the agreement's client money history whose reason is a returned payment, dated in the 3 months before the payoff. A reversal for an overpayment refund does not count. A window of a number of months before a date covers the dates after the same day that number of months earlier, up to and including that date; here the window ends on the day of the payoff.

**What does it reduce?**
The late charges that enter the payoff. The concessions that apply are first added into one share, never more than the whole, and the late charges that enter are reduced once by that share; the unpaid amount itself is never reduced. The payoff is the unpaid amount plus the reduced late charges, rounded to the cent once at the end.

| Returned-payment reversals on the agreement, 3 months before the payoff | Concession |
|---|---|
| 2 or more | 10 percent |
| exactly 1 | 5 percent |
| none | nothing |

**A worked case (hypothetical inputs).**
Payoff on 2026-08-12, with returned-payment reversals dated 2026-05-12 and 2026-07-03 and an overpayment-refund reversal dated 2026-07-20. The reversal of 2026-05-12 lies on the same day 3 months earlier and falls outside the window; the overpayment refund does not count. One reversal counts, so the concession is 5 percent. On an unpaid amount of 900.00 USD and late charges entering of 40.00 USD, with only this concession applying, the payoff is 900.00 USD plus 38.00 USD, which is 938.00 USD.
